info.title: Didit Auth API
info.description:
Programmatic registration and authentication API for developers and AI agents. Register in 2 API calls -- no browser needed. The most agent-friendly identity verification platform.

## Base URL

All endpoints in this spec are hosted at `https://apx.didit.me/auth/v2`. This is a different host than the verification API (`https://verification.didit.me/v3`). Keep them straight: this auth host issues your **JWT access tokens** and lets you list and manage your **organizations** and **applications**. The verification host is where you call sessions, workflows, AML, etc., authenticated with the **`api_key`** returned by this API.

## How the auth flow works

1. `POST /programmatic/register/`: submit email + password.
2. Receive a 6-character alphanumeric code by email.
3. `POST /programmatic/verify-email/`: submit the code. You get back a JWT `access_token`, a `refresh_token`, an organization and two applications, each with `client_id` + `api_key`: `sandbox_application` (free, every check is mocked and never billed) and `application` (live, every check is billed from the organization's balance, which starts at $0).
4. Save both `api_key` values. Build and test with the sandbox key as `x-api-key` on every call to `https://verification.didit.me/v3/...`, and switch to the live `application` key only to go live, after adding credit.
5. From any future machine, `POST /programmatic/login/` exchanges your email + password for a fresh JWT, then call `GET /organizations/me/` and the application endpoints to recover or rotate credentials.

The JWT is only needed for the **Account Management** endpoints in this spec; verification API traffic uses the long-lived `api_key`, not the JWT.

## Conventions

- All request and response bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).
- **Use a real, deliverable email address when testing `POST /programmatic/register/`.** The address is checked before any account is created: addresses on reserved test domains (`@example.com`, `@example.org`, `@*.test`, `@*.example`, `@*.invalid`) and others that cannot receive the code return `400` with `"code": "email_undeliverable"` and a `reason`. Substitute the `you@yourdomain.com` placeholder in the samples with an inbox you can actually read.
- Validation errors return HTTP `400` with one of two envelopes: `{"field": ["message", ...]}` for field-level problems, or `{"detail": "message"}` for business-rule errors. A handful of validators (password strength on register, code expiry on verify-email) currently respond with a bare array `["message"]` instead of the field-keyed form -- this is a known server-side inconsistency, so client code should accept both shapes.
- Authentication errors come back as `{"detail": "..."}` with HTTP `401` (invalid bearer token) or `403` (missing bearer token / insufficient privileges).
- Rate-limit responses include a `wait` field with the cooldown in seconds.

## Console identity recovery

Identity actions are console-only and require a console session; account API tokens, application API keys and end-user access tokens do not grant access. They are not public server SDK operations. See [admin identity actions](https://docs.didit.me/authentication/sign-in-methods#admin-identity-actions) for reset MFA, sign-in links, password reset and bulk status changes. The x-console-identity-actions extension references their request and result schemas without adding callable SDK paths.

tags.description: Email-and-password account lifecycle: register, verify, login. Returns the JWT `access_token` you use against the Account Management endpoints, plus (on verify) your first application's `client_id` and `api_key`.

tags.description: Authenticated endpoints (JWT bearer) that list organizations and create, fetch, or update applications. Use these to recover or rotate the `api_key` you authenticate verification API calls with.

tags.name: Setup
tags.description: Set up Didit Authentication by API: the sign-in methods, the application settings, branding, bot protection, verified sign-in, the sign-up emails, the hosted domain and the native apps. These routes live on `https://apx.didit.me/auth/v2/organizations/{organization_id}/applications/{application_id}/authentication/`, not on the application's issuer, and they take a credential an owner approved: a management grant, or a named API key with the `authentication` scope. The console session of an owner or admin with `write:authentication` still works. End-user data, organizations, roles, imports and agent sessions stay console-only.

post.description: Step 1 of programmatic onboarding. Creates a pending account and emails a 6-char code (10 min TTL). The address is checked before any account is created: one that cannot receive the code returns 400 `email_undeliverable`. Rate limits: 5/IP/hour, plus a shared hourly budget per network (/24 for IPv4, /64 for IPv6).

200.description: An account with this email is already registered but not verified yet. A new 6-character verification code was emailed (valid for 10 minutes) and nothing else changes: the password sent in this request is ignored. Call `POST /programmatic/verify-email/` next with the new code.

value.message: A new verification code has been sent to your email.

201.description: Registration successful. A 6-character alphanumeric verification code (e.g., `A3K9F2`) was emailed to the supplied address and is valid for 10 minutes. Call `POST /programmatic/verify-email/` next.

value.message: Registration successful. Check your email for the verification code.

400.description: Validation error. The intended envelope is `{"field": ["..."]}` for field-level errors and `{"detail": "..."}` for business-rule errors (e.g. duplicate email). Password-strength rules currently respond with a bare array `["..."]`, one rule at a time -- known server-side inconsistency; treat it as `{"password": ["..."]}` until fixed. When the address cannot receive the code (disposable, reserved or test domain, no mail server, a likely typo, or a previously bounced address), the body is `EmailUndeliverableError` with `code: "email_undeliverable"`; no account is created or changed.

Also returned, with a `Retry-After: 5` header, when the service is momentarily checking as many passwords or codes as it can at once; retry after the indicated number of seconds.

200.description: Email verified. The response contains tokens for this auth API plus the brand-new application's `client_id` and `api_key`. Persist the `api_key` securely — it is the long-lived credential used by every verification API call. When the account already has an authenticator app or a passkey, the response carries `2fa_required: true`, a `temp_token`, `has_authenticator` and `has_passkeys` instead of tokens and application keys: finish the sign-in with the second factor, then read the organization and its applications from `/organizations/me/`.

post.description:
Create an application inside an organization, in the data location you choose (`data_location`, the European Union by default; it can't be changed afterwards). The response includes `api_key`; persist it now (recoverable via GET). Requires owner/admin JWT.

Set initiate_login_uri to your HTTPS sign-in page on the exact website_url hostname, or an empty string to disable admin-sent sign-in links. Changing website_url also revalidates the saved sign-in URI. Invalid values return 400 with an initiate_login_uri field error; hostname and URI policy failures use https_url_on_registered_website_required. An MCP token (a "Log in with Didit" grant, `token_use` `mcp`) also needs the `didit:management` scope, which carries the `applications` resource; a grant limited to `didit:verification` is refused with 403 before anything is created.

parameters.description: UUID of the organization. Look it up with `GET /organizations/me/`.

requestBody.description: All fields are optional. Omitting the body creates an application with default name `"<organization name> App"` and no public URLs configured.

201.description: Application created. The response includes the long-lived `api_key`; persist it now and use it as the `x-api-key` header on every `https://verification.didit.me/v3/...` call.

400.description: Validation error in the request body: for example a malformed redirect URI, a `data_location` that is not available yet (`au`, `mx`, `ae`, `us`) or one that does not exist. Nothing is created.

403.description: You cannot create applications in this organization. A token issued to an AI agent (MCP) whose consent does not include application management gets `This token's scope does not permit this action.`, and a token limited to verification cannot read or change applications or their API keys. An MCP token whose grant lacks the `applications` resource (for example one limited to `didit:verification`, or `didit:staff` alone) gets `This token's scope does not permit this action.`.

patch.description:
Update application metadata (name, URLs, redirect URIs). `api_key` and `client_id` are never rotated. `products` is read-only: a `products` key in the body is ignored. `data_location` can't be changed after the application is created, except once on the live application created with your organization, while it is unused (see the request body). Requires owner/admin JWT.

Set initiate_login_uri to your HTTPS sign-in page on the exact website_url hostname, or an empty string to disable admin-sent sign-in links. Changing website_url also revalidates the saved sign-in URI. Invalid values return 400 with an initiate_login_uri field error; hostname and URI policy failures use https_url_on_registered_website_required.
